brief: Today is 28 November and tonight is Pull A. Last night's Push A was the build card again, because your phone's phase is still locked to Meso 3. Smith incline went to 185 for 8, 8, a new best at this gym; laterals 17.5 for 15 on every set you logged; and your first neck flexion was 10 lb for 12, 12. Three things did not hold: the crossover at 17.5 (10 reps, then 15.5 for 12, 12), the chest press at 172.5 (8 on the first set, under Push A's 10 to 12), and the fourth lateral set, missed for the second time. Your note asked where the neck flexion field guide is. The card should have had one; the app's guide sheet only reads the original lift list. I filed that as an app bug, and the guide is in my answer below your notes. One program change today, version 19. On both push nights with four lateral sets you did three, so each push day now asks three, and three sets of cable lateral raise go on the end of Pull A, the 10 lb you did there on 10 November. Side delts are what make the shoulders look wide on stage, and they have been getting 7 sets a week against a floor of 10; this makes it 9 direct, and 3 more than you have actually been doing. It is a third lateral day, which on 12 November you said felt like every day; it is three days of six, and side delts recover fast enough for it. What your phone shows tonight under the lock, from the app's own rules (I did not set these): deadlift 215, 235, 245 and 250, all for 6; wide pulldown 112.5, 127.5 and 135, all for 10; seated row 112.5 for 12, four sets; dumbbell curl 35 for 10, three sets; hammer curl 42.5 for 12, three sets; face pulls 32.5 for 15, two sets; cable lateral raise 10 for 15, three sets. Several of those are a rep or two past your best at this gym: deadlift 245 and 250 for 6 (you did 5), pulldown 135 for 10 (you did 8), row 12s at 112.5 (you did 10s), curl 35 for 10 (you did 8s). This review's numbers, which reach your card only with the phase on Automatic, follow the calendar's lighter week, 20% off with about 60% of the sets: deadlift 190 then 200 for 5; wide pulldown 97.5 then 105 for 8; row 90 for 10, two sets; curl 25 for 8, two sets; hammer curl 30 for 10, two sets; face pulls 25 for 12, one set; cable lateral raise 5 for 12, two sets. That is a change from yesterday's numbers, which kept your full weights. This is the last lighter week before the cut, and assessment from 2 December should measure what you can do, not nine weeks of fatigue. One question: is the Meso 3 lock deliberate? If it is, say so in a note and I will write the reviews knowing the build card is what you train. Dates: lighter week ends 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, show 1 March, 93 days away. Still needed: a morning bodyweight (nothing since 23 August, 207 lb; the Bodyweight button on the workout screen) and your division.

Smith incline 185 for 8, 8 (a new best here), laterals 17.5 for 15 on every set logged, dips 11, 12, 12 and the first neck flexion, 10 lb for 12, 12. Three things did not hold: the crossover at 17.5 (10 reps, then 15.5 for 12), the chest press at 172.5 (8 on the first set, under Push A's 10 to 12) and the fourth lateral set (three of four, as on 23 November). That is two nights inside the lighter week (25 November to 1 December) trained at full build sets, 25 and 27 November. This is the last lighter week before an eleven-and-a-half-week cut, and assessment (2 to 8 December) reads your best reps at current weights; if you arrive at it after nine straight build weeks, it measures fatigue, not what you can do. So this review's loads follow the calendar's own rule (20% off, about 60% of the sets), the numbers the app itself gives with the phase on Automatic. Sets hold; the weights move. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 18 planned a week, of which 18 are direct sets; 13.5 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

The dose-response research (roughly 10 to 20 hard sets per muscle a week, Schoenfeld, Ogborn and Krieger 2017) puts 18 inside the range, and the row keeps adding load at every visit, so the four stay; a note on the card changes that. Both rows are going up: seated row 112.5 for 10 on all four on 16 November, chest-supported row 60 for 10 on all four on 24 November (9 on 13 November). Hold. prep.plan: Eleven days come before prep (from 28 November). The build block ended on 24 November; your phone has kept running build cards since (25 and 27 November) because its phase is locked to Meso 3. The calendar calls 25 November to 1 December a lighter week; this review's cards are two sets of proven weights, but your phone's phase is locked to Meso 3, so the app runs its own build numbers instead (see the block). While that lock stays, assessment and prep reviews are set aside the same way, so this plan reaches your card only with the phase on Automatic. The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts and weights as now, with the sets as they stand after the side-delt decision (2 December review) and the second calf lift added on 26 November; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 23 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (24 February to 1 March, show day): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the 11 days before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters now and not in December. The prep phase in the calendar is a placeholder that detailed programming replaces at assessment, so this plan is a default, not a decision. What it protects, in order, once real data arrives: side delts, upper chest (Push A), back, arms, quads, calves; the deadlift is climbing 5 to 10 lb a visit (250 for 5 on 16 November) and the RDL is climbing in reps at 185 (8, 9, then 10 on 7, 14 and 25 November) and in a deficit they hold their weight rather than climb. If no bodyweight arrives by 2 December, I will start prep on 9 December from 207 lb (23 August) and say so. Assessment (2 to 8 December) reads each main lift at its current weight for its best reps; if two of them come in under their reps of 15 to 25 November, prep starts with sets coming off the least-scored muscles at once, not in week 5. In prep, a cut in sets is triggered by any week where two or more main lifts fall below their previous reps or where a session ends with its late slots skipped. Three things a stage plan needs that this one does not yet have, and that wait on your answers: when posing practice starts (most competitors start about 12 weeks out, which is now), whether cardio is used for fat loss or food alone, and how the last week (water, food, the pump-up) is run, which depends on your division and whoever sets your diet. If a bodyweight arrives before 2 December and shows more to lose than the 12 to 23 lb this pace allows, the deficit should start at assessment rather than on 9 December. A week with lighter loads (20% off, two thirds of the sets) is set for prep week 6 (13 to 19 January) if two or more main lifts fall below their previous reps in the two weeks before it.

answers.answer: You are right, the card was missing it, and the cause is the app, not you. I wrote a guide for neck flexion into the program on 19 November, but the app's guide sheet reads only the original lift list, and the four lifts added through the program (neck flexion, neck extension, overhead triceps extension, ab crunch machine) all show "No field guide for this one." I cannot change the app's code; I filed it as an app bug (how-to-sheet-misses-program-lifts) so it gets fixed. Until then, the guide: lie on your back on a flat bench with your head and neck off the end, fold a towel over your forehead and hold the plate flat on it with both hands. Let your head drop back slowly until you feel a stretch in the front of your neck, without forcing it. Bring your chin up toward your chest under control, pause for a beat, and lower again, with no jerking and no bouncing at the bottom. Keep the 10 lb and build the reps: 12 last time, toward 20; the weight goes up only after both sets reach 20 with no neck soreness the next day. With your phase locked, the app's next card will ask 20, 20; 15 is a sensible next step.
